newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical industry reduces pollution output.
newsitem.headline: German chemical industry reduces pollution output.

text.p: The German chemical industry has spent 37 billion marks in five years on environmental measures, managing to significantly reduce pollution, an industry federation said on Monday.

In a report on enviromental measures, the industry federation VCI said companies had spent 9.15 billion marks on investments and a total of 37 billion marks to operate new plants, clean up waste and monitor developments between 1989 and 1994.

During that time emissions from chemical plants dropped significantly, the VCI said, noting sulphur dioxide emissions dropped by 90 percent while nitrogen dioxide emissions were reduced by 72 percent.
At the same time the industry association also said that safety at chemical plants had improved continuously over the last 15 years.
